hints: Focus on partial pressures, not moles, since Kp uses the pressure of each gas at equilibrium.
First find total moles (930 mol) and use mole fraction x total pressure to get each partial pressure.
Put those pressures into the Kp expression for the forward reaction and check the powers and units carefully to finish.
walkthrough:
**Write the Kp expression**

Remember Kp uses partial pressures raised to the powers in the balanced equation. Products go on top.

$$K_p = \frac{(p_{NH_3})^2}{p_{N_2} \times (p_{H_2})^3}$$

**Find total moles and mole fractions**

First add up all the equilibrium moles to share out the total pressure fairly.

$$n_{total} = 180 + 590 + 160 = 930 \text{ mol}$$

$$x = \frac{n}{n_{total}}$$

So $x_{N_2} = 180/930$, $x_{H_2} = 590/930$, $x_{NH_3} = 160/930$.

**Convert to partial pressures**

Multiply each mole fraction by the total pressure of 300 atm.

$$p = x \times p_{total}$$

$$p_{N_2} = \frac{180}{930} \times 300 = 58.06 \text{ atm}$$

$$p_{H_2} = \frac{590}{930} \times 300 = 190.3 \text{ atm}$$

$$p_{NH_3} = \frac{160}{930} \times 300 = 51.61 \text{ atm}$$

**Substitute and calculate Kp**

Pop the three partial pressures into the expression, remembering to square ammonia and cube hydrogen.

$$K_p = \frac{(51.61)^2}{58.06 \times (190.3)^3} = 6.65 \times 10^{-6}$$

Units are $\text{atm}^{2-1-3} = \text{atm}^{-2}$. This matches the forward reaction.

options.A: Correct. Using partial pressures p(N2)=58.06 atm, p(H2)=190.3 atm, p(NH3)=51.61 atm gives Kp = (51.61)^2 / [58.06 x (190.3)^3] = 6.65 x 10^-6 atm^-2.
options.B: Incorrect. This value is about 10 times too large. It often comes from an arithmetic slip, such as rounding partial pressures too early or mishandling the large (pH2)^3 term in the denominator.
options.C: Incorrect. This comes from putting moles directly into the Kp expression instead of partial pressures, or forgetting to multiply by total pressure correctly. Kp must use partial pressures in atm, not mol.
options.D: Incorrect. This is essentially 1 / Kp for the forward reaction, the Kp for the reverse decomposition of ammonia. It has inverted units of atm^2 because products and reactants have been swapped.
